title: Wallabag read schema includes a sensitive client secret
reasoning: WallabagConfigRead is the public read response schema and explicitly treats the password as masked, but it still includes client_secret as a plain string. OAuth client secrets are credentials too, so endpoints returning this schema can disclose a stored secret to callers who only need to view configuration state.
recommendation: Mask or omit client_secret from WallabagConfigRead, matching the password handling. If clients need to know whether a secret exists, expose a boolean such as has_client_secret instead.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked API/schema tests were provided, and there is no evidence here that read responses assert secret masking for client_secret.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a response-schema or endpoint test for reading Wallabag config that stores a non-empty client_secret and asserts the returned payload does not contain the raw secret.
minimumFixScope: Update WallabagConfigRead and the config read mapping code to omit or mask client_secret, plus adjust any frontend/API consumers expecting the raw value.
